results.title: [Feedback] Guild Note APIs (GuildRosterSetPublicNote / C_GuildInfo.SetNote) and Secret Values - UI and Macro - World of Warcraft Forums
excerpts:
World of Warcraft Forums

# [[Feedback] Guild Note APIs (GuildRosterSetPublicNote / C\_GuildInfo.SetNote) and Secret Values](/en/wow/t/feedback-guild-note-apis-guildrostersetpublicnote-cguildinfosetnote-and-secret-values/615202)

Guides UI and Macro

[GameStreaker-1518496](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/GameStreaker-1518496) (GameStreaker) April 8, 2026, 9:32pm 1

Hello everyone,

I’d like to open a discussion about the guild note APIs and their current state since Patch 12.0.

I’m the developer of **Gilden-Tool** , a guild management addon that has been active since BfA. Its core function is simple: it writes a compact info string into the player’s **own public guild note** containing their name, item level, and role (e.g. `"PlayerName 630 Tank"` ).

Since Patch 12.0, this is no longer possible. The following APIs are now silently blocked for addon code:

* `GuildRosterSetPublicNote()`
* `GuildRosterSetOfficerNote()`
* `C_GuildInfo.SetNote()`
Calls from addon code are dropped without any error message. Known workarounds (hooking the note editor, event-based timing, clipboard access) all fail due to the taint system.

**Why I think this is worth discussing**

The stated goal of the Secret Values system is to limit addon automation around combat information. Writing a guild note is a purely social and organizational feature. Guild notes are not visible during encounters, they provide no competitive advantage, and they cannot influence gameplay decisions.

This feels similar to other non-combat APIs that were restored after community feedback, such as loot council communication, raid note sharing, and break timers.

**Who is affected**

Several addons that serve guild communities rely on this functionality:

* **Gilden-Tool** \- auto-updates public note with name, iLvl, and role
* **GuildNoteUpdater** \- similar functionality, discontinued due to this restriction
* **GuildNoteSetter** and other guild management tools
These addons help guild leaders keep rosters organized, especially in large guilds where members frequently switch specs or gear. Without them, every guild member has to manually update their note after every gear or spec change. In practice, this means most notes end up outdated or empty.

**A possible solution**

One approach could be to whitelist the guild note APIs from Secret Value restrictions. Alternatively, a new API that allows addons to write to only the player’s own guild note could be a reasonable middle ground, keeping the restriction in place for modifying other members’ notes.

**Some additional context**

* The affected addons only write to the player’s own note (no reading of combat data, no gameplay automation)
* The guild note system is a social feature used for organization, not combat
* Other guild-related read APIs ( `GetGuildRosterInfo` , `GetNumGuildMembers` , `IsInGuild` ) continue to work as expected

The first three games in the _Warcraft_ series, including their expansion packs, were all released on both the PC and Macintosh . All of these games were of the real-time strategy genre. Each game proceeded to carry on the storyline of the previous games, and each introduced new features and content to improve gameplay. The name "Warcraft" was proposed by Blizzard developer Sam Didier. It was chosen because "it sounded super cool", according to Blizzard co-founder Allen Adham , without any particular meaning attached to it. [[ 9 ]]()

_Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness_ was the first game in the series to feature play over the internet using Battle.

...

The third continent, Northrend, is located in the northern polar region of Azeroth and is the primary stronghold of the malevolent Undead Scourge. Northrend is featured in _Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos_ and its expansion set _Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne_ , and is the main location featured in _World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King_ , the second expansion pack to _World of Warcraft_ . [[ 4 ]]()

In the expansion _World of Warcraft: Cataclysm_ , Azeroth has been changed permanently in-game, even for players without the expansion set installed. The corrupted Black Dragon Aspect, Deathwing the Destroyer (formerly Neltharion, the Earth-Warder) has broken free from imprisonment in Deepholm, part of the Elemental Plane, and caused major changes and destruction in the land. In addition, many new parts of the continents of Azeroth that have previously been inaccessible have become key parts in the new world.

...

The tenth expansion, _World of Warcraft: The War Within_ , takes players beneath the surface of Azeroth into the subterranean kingdom of Khaz Algar, home of the Earthen, a new playable allied race. The expansion introduces Warbands, an account-wide system for sharing currencies, collections, and reputations across characters, as well as Delves, a new form of solo instanced content.

The eleventh expansion, _World of Warcraft: Midnight_ , [[ 39 ]]() returns to the elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas , introducing four new zones including Eversong and Zul'Aman. The expansion features three raids, eight new dungeons, and a player housing system — the first in the game's twenty-year history.
